html:
A revolt in 1898 against a new British tax on every dwelling in the Sierra Leone Protectorate, declared over the interior in 1896.

In the north the Temne chief Bai Bureh fought a skilled guerrilla war for months before he was captured in November and exiled to the Gold Coast. In the south, Mende fighters organised through the Poro society killed hundreds of people seen as agents of the colony, including missionaries and Krio traders. The British put the revolt down hard and hanged nearly a hundred men. The tax stayed. Bai Bureh became a national hero. See also British rule.
sum: A revolt in 1898 against a new British tax on every dwelling in the Sierra Leone Protectorate, declared over the interior in 1896.
